answer: The most enriched process in the ASXL1-mutated fibroblasts is cell adhesion (GO:0007155-class). Differential expression (DESeq2-style median-of-ratios size factors + per-gene negative-binomial GLM, design ~ sex + condition, BH FDR) identified 1,066 significantly upregulated genes in the mutant ("disease") fibroblasts (padj<0.05, log2FC>0; 599 with log2FC>=1) versus 497 downregulated. Over-representation of the upregulated genes against the expression-detected background (19,581 genes) showed cell adhesion as the single most enriched biological process by a wide margin: 59 of 306 adhesion-class genes hit, one-sided Fisher p = 1.2e-17, BH-adjusted p = 1.6e-16, with prominent cadherins/protocadherins, contactins, ephrins, adhesion GPCRs (ADGRB2/ADGRL1-3/ADGRE2), integrins and junction genes (CLDN1, CXADR, ALCAM, CDH1, VCAM1). The next most enriched process was extracellular matrix organization (p = 8.1e-06), far behind. The result is robust to a stricter log2FC>=1 threshold (cell adhesion p = 3.8e-10, again top). Sensitivity check on the downregulated set points to a different top term (ECM organization), confirming direction specificity.
